Build TESSERA v2 in this repo following uploads/V2-HANDOFF.md exactly. That file is the builder brief, with the goal, architecture, ordered PR list V2-001…V2-062 with acceptance tests, and the hard limits. Context files are TESSERA-V2-PLAN.md (full plan plus sources appendix), V2-FEATURE-MAP.csv, v2-memory.jsonl (an MCP memory-server knowledge graph of all inputs, which you load with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` and MEMORY_FILE_PATH, and query instead of re-reading everything), and REA-COVERAGE-V2.md.

Work rules: one small PR per plan item, each in order, each with tests that pass locally (CI is blocked by GitHub billing, so put the local test output in every PR body as proof). Merge each PR into main once its tests pass and it's rebased on main; Father has standing approval for tested work. Commit as `vitalitychems-dot <332565808+vitalitychems-dot@users.noreply.github.com>`, never as Tessera.

Hard limits: no wallets, payments, crypto, mining or trading code; nothing from 1T or vault; no deletes of repos, data or history; no history rewrites; no TESSERA_ENABLE_* flag flips; nothing from the excluded categories (captcha solving, bot-detection bypass, antidetect, credential cracking, people-OSINT); and no wholesale copies of Zz or olive. Only reuse code under a compatible license, with attribution.

After each 10 PRs, append to docs/v2/BUILD-LOG.md with: number, PR, a plain-words description and the merge SHA. Final report: every PR with its merge SHA and test results, plus anything skipped and why.

# V2-HANDOFF — Build brief for Tessera Builder
**For:** Cursor cloud agent on `vitalitychems-dot/TESSERA`  
**From:** Phase-1 planner (2026-10-12 CT)  
**Companion files (read these first):
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/REA-COVERAGE-V2.md` — REA % per repo**
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/TESSERA-V2-PLAN.md` — full architecture & sources
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/V2-FEATURE-MAP.csv` — every inventory repo → include/exclude
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/v2-memory.jsonl` — MCP memory graph (entities/relations)
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/SECURITY-PROTOCOLS-INVENTORY.md`
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/OFFLINE-INTERNET.md`
- REA outputs: `/workspace/rea-batch/v2-rea-out/*.json` and `/workspace/rea-batch/b2-out/*.json`

---

## 1. Goal (one paragraph)

Build **TESSERA v2** inside `vitalitychems-dot/TESSERA`: an MIT (default) all-in-one open-source Tessera where a **lead agent (Tessera)** plans on a visible **studio board**, **worker agents** each get a **desk + git worktree + sandbox**, the app works **offline** on an **encrypted mesh**, adapters call taught sites / sanctioned APIs, and a **knowledge graph + token lab** cut re-reads and tokens. Combine useful ideas from ~315 inventory names; **never** import excluded categories.

---

## 2. Architecture (what to build)

1. **Studio / Foreman (AgentCraft model, clean-room or MIT-attributed)**  
   - Lead = Tessera pen (xAI/Grok now; GLM-5 later when TESTED).  
   - Workers = mesh lanes.  
   - Task graph, decisions, shared memory, **approve-only merge**, **no git push** for agents.  
   - **Web 2D studio required**; optional 3D; Minecraft **not** required.

2. **TESSERA preview + api-server** — keep existing `offline/`, `mesh-node/`, `secure-mesh/`, `tessera/` (memory-web, token-graph, local-learn, shepherd, sovereign-fetch-guard).

3. **GitMesh** (ex-GitbookAI) — git-carried public drops. **Gitbook** — intake/mesh/merge docs.

4. **Adapters** — sanctioned MCP first; optional `goodnight000/api-anything` (MIT) for public no-login sites; cookies import **OFF**.

5. **Compute** — per-desk sandbox, CPU/mem limits, **network denied by default**.

6. **Knowledge graph** — MCP memory JSONL shape; agents query entities/relations/observations instead of whole-file re-reads. Flowsint (Apache-2.0) = **UX reference only**; no people-OSINT.

7. **Token lab** — baseline meter; A/B: graph retrieval, summary cache, diff-only context, small-model routing, prompt compression, memoized tool results.

---

## 3. Ordered PR list (implement in order; each must pass local tests before merge)

### A — Foundations
| ID | Work | Acceptance test |
|---|---|---|
| V2-001 | HYB-011 denylist (routes/files) | Fixture requests to wallet/payment/vault/1T patterns → refused |
| V2-002 | MIT LICENSE + NOTICE | Files exist; package.json license MIT |
| V2-003 | Vendor plan snapshot under `docs/v2/` (feature map summary + memory pointer) | JSONL schema parse test |
| V2-004 | REA coverage markdown from v2-rea-out/*.cov | Table rendered in docs |

### B — Agents studio
| ID | Work | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| V2-010 | TaskGraph + DecisionQueue (sim) | Unit: dependency gating + decision blocks worker |
| V2-011 | git worktree per task | create/cleanup; `git push` fails in worktree hooks |
| V2-012 | Merge gate | merge only after approve; dirty main refuses |
| V2-013 | WS protocol schemas | schema check script green |
| V2-014 | Web 2D Task Wall + desks | Playwright: post goal → cards |
| V2-015 | Optional 3D flag (default off) | build passes with flag off |
| V2-016 | Lead planner adapter (sim + pen hook) | sim run completes 2-task goal |
| V2-017 | Worker log → monitor stream | fake worker events visible in API |

### C — Offline mesh
| ID | Work | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| V2-020 | O1 file-mesh index ≥50 | query returns Gitbook-derived hit `live:false` |
| V2-021 | O2 offlineQueue | fake-indexeddb replay once |
| V2-022 | O3 SW shell | sw.js emitted; offline navigation shell |
| V2-023 | O7 badge | component test |
| V2-024 | O10 mesh-node | existing unit tests + e2e join/leave log |
| V2-025 | O11 secure-mesh | encrypt/decrypt + bad sig reject |
| V2-026 | O5 sneakernet script | bundle round-trip sha |
| V2-027 | O6 LAN P2P | unit config |
| V2-028 | O4 Kiwix optional | mock HTTP; default off |
| V2-029 | O8 Gitbook page | (docs PR on Gitbook if needed) |
| V2-030 | O9 LoRa note | doc only |

### D — Knowledge + Flowsint-inspired UI
| ID | Work | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| V2-040 | Unify KG store | `open_nodes`-style query API |
| V2-041 | MCP memory config | server read_graph non-empty |
| V2-042 | Library graph panel | renders task/doc nodes; **no** external OSINT enrichers |
| V2-043 | Own-repo metadata enricher | only `vitalitychems-dot/*` |

### E — Compute + token lab
| ID | Work | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| V2-050 | Desk sandbox | network denied; mem limit enforced in test harness |
| V2-051 | Token baseline meter | metrics JSON after fixture task |
| V2-052 | A/B graph retrieval | both arms recorded |
| V2-053 | Summary cache + diff-only | token count decreases on cache hit |
| V2-054 | Small-model routing + compression | router unit test |
| V2-055 | Proposal queue for new methods | schema validation; no auto-enable |

### F — Adapters + UI
| ID | Work | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| V2-060 | api-anything allowlist adapter | HN fixture; login/cookies disabled |
| V2-061 | Chamber/Board + duplicate-guard | UI + guard tests |
| V2-062 | GitMesh string cleanup | no user-facing "GitbookAI" |

**Do not open PRs that combine studio + mesh + token lab in one shot.** One ID per PR.

---

## 4. Hard limits (stop and ask Father if tempted)

- **No** wallets, payments, trading/MEV/DeFi bots, mining, NFT, captcha solvers, Cloudflare/bot-detection bypass, antidetect/stealth browsers, hashcat/cracking, browser fingerprinting libs.  
- **No** `1T` or `vault` paths (read, copy, or import).  
- **No** deleting repos or archive folders.  
- **No** git history rewrites.  
- **No** flipping `TESSERA_ENABLE*` (or equivalent) feature flags.  
- **No** executing code from cloned third-party/archive apps — read/REA/port patterns only.  
- **No** people-OSINT (Flowsint enrichers against persons).  
- **No** OpenAI as default pen (GB-052).  
- **No** deploying archived XXX income/arbitrage/wallet routes.  
- Vitality store stays out of the combine.

---

## 5. Commit identity & CI

- Author/committer: **vitalitychems-dot** GitHub noreply (`vitalitychems-dot@users.noreply.github.com` or the account’s configured noreply).  
- **CI is blocked by billing** → green **local** `pnpm test` / package tests are the merge proof. Paste test output in the PR body.  
- Prefer small commits; PR title `V2-0xx: …`.  
- Do not force-push main; do not use `--no-verify` unless Father says so.

---

## 6. How to load the full picture (mandatory before coding)

```bash
export PATH=/workspace/tools/node22/bin:$PATH
export MEMORY_FILE_PATH=/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/v2-memory.jsonl
# MCP: npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
# Then read_graph / search_nodes for TESSERA_v2, module_*, decision_*, risk_*
```

Also open:
- Feature map CSV (include/exclude reasons).  
- Latest `v2-rea-out/*.cov` coverage lines.  
- Gitbook `merge/HYB-011-EXCLUSION-MANIFEST.md` and `merge/CONSOLIDATION-MAP-2026-10-12.md` (from clone).

---

## 7. REA coverage expectations

Re-run or read:

| Repo / tree | Role | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| TESSERA | base | Expect ~95%+ JS parse |
| Gitbook novault stage | docs+archives | 1T/vault excluded; Zz imports/trees included in tree |
| GitMesh | mesh drops | small |
| vitality | **risk flags only** | do not merge store into Tessera |
| Zz / XXX / olive / T44 | capability mine | exclude wallet routes when porting |

After any new REA, append entities `rea::<name>` into `v2-memory.jsonl` (or regenerate via planner script) so the next agent sees coverage %.

---

## 8. Definition of done for “v2 MVP”

- Studio sim backend: goal → ≥2 tasks → worktrees → tests → approve merge.  
- Offline: index ≥50 pages, queue replay, SW shell, mesh encrypt unit green.  
- KG queryable via MCP memory.  
- Token baseline meter writing metrics.  
- HYB-011 denylist TESTED.  
- No excluded-category code paths introduced.

---

## 9. Father cadence

Auto-continue within limits; every **100 actions** produce a numbered list of what shipped. Father says **yes** (keep all) or lists IDs to undo.

---

## 10. Quick commands

```bash
export PATH=/workspace/tools/node22/bin:$PATH
cd /path/to/TESSERA
pnpm test   # or package-scoped tests — local proof
# REA one tree:
npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0 analyze-javascript-application <dir> --json
```

# V2-HANDOFF — Build brief for Tessera Builder
**For:** Cursor cloud agent on `vitalitychems-dot/TESSERA`  
**From:** Phase-1 planner (2026-10-12 CT)  
**Companion files (read these first):
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/REA-COVERAGE-V2.md` — REA % per repo**
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/TESSERA-V2-PLAN.md` — full architecture & sources
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/V2-FEATURE-MAP.csv` — every inventory repo → include/exclude
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/v2-memory.jsonl` — MCP memory graph (entities/relations)
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/SECURITY-PROTOCOLS-INVENTORY.md`
- `/workspace/build-plan-2026-10-12/OFFLINE-INTERNET.md`
- REA outputs: `/workspace/rea-batch/v2-rea-out/*.json` and `/workspace/rea-batch/b2-out/*.json`

---

## 1. Goal (one paragraph)

Build **TESSERA v2** inside `vitalitychems-dot/TESSERA`: an MIT (default) all-in-one open-source Tessera where a **lead agent (Tessera)** plans on a visible **studio board**, **worker agents** each get a **desk + git worktree + sandbox**, the app works **offline** on an **encrypted mesh**, adapters call taught sites / sanctioned APIs, and a **knowledge graph + token lab** cut re-reads and tokens. Combine useful ideas from ~315 inventory names; **never** import excluded categories.

---

## 2. Architecture (what to build)

1. **Studio / Foreman (AgentCraft model, clean-room or MIT-attributed)**  
   - Lead = Tessera pen (xAI/Grok now; GLM-5 later when TESTED).  
   - Workers = mesh lanes.  
   - Task graph, decisions, shared memory, **approve-only merge**, **no git push** for agents.  
   - **Web 2D studio required**; optional 3D; Minecraft **not** required.

2. **TESSERA preview + api-server** — keep existing `offline/`, `mesh-node/`, `secure-mesh/`, `tessera/` (memory-web, token-graph, local-learn, shepherd, sovereign-fetch-guard).

3. **GitMesh** (ex-GitbookAI) — git-carried public drops. **Gitbook** — intake/mesh/merge docs.

4. **Adapters** — sanctioned MCP first; optional `goodnight000/api-anything` (MIT) for public no-login sites; cookies import **OFF**.

5. **Compute** — per-desk sandbox, CPU/mem limits, **network denied by default**.

6. **Knowledge graph** — MCP memory JSONL shape; agents query entities/relations/observations instead of whole-file re-reads. Flowsint (Apache-2.0) = **UX reference only**; no people-OSINT.

7. **Token lab** — baseline meter; A/B: graph retrieval, summary cache, diff-only context, small-model routing, prompt compression, memoized tool results.

---

## 3. Ordered PR list (implement in order; each must pass local tests before merge)

### A — Foundations
| ID | Work | Acceptance test |
|---|---|---|
| V2-001 | HYB-011 denylist (routes/files) | Fixture requests to wallet/payment/vault/1T patterns → refused |
| V2-002 | MIT LICENSE + NOTICE | Files exist; package.json license MIT |
| V2-003 | Vendor plan snapshot under `docs/v2/` (feature map summary + memory pointer) | JSONL schema parse test |
| V2-004 | REA coverage markdown from v2-rea-out/*.cov | Table rendered in docs |

### B — Agents studio
| ID | Work | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| V2-010 | TaskGraph + DecisionQueue (sim) | Unit: dependency gating + decision blocks worker |
| V2-011 | git worktree per task | create/cleanup; `git push` fails in worktree hooks |
| V2-012 | Merge gate | merge only after approve; dirty main refuses |
| V2-013 | WS protocol schemas | schema check script green |
| V2-014 | Web 2D Task Wall + desks | Playwright: post goal → cards |

+# Offline Internet
+
+When the network is down, Tessera still answers from pages already carried in the git mesh.
+
+- The file index searches those pages and marks each hit `live: false`.
+- Writes wait in a local queue and replay once the link returns.
+- The app shell is cached so the studio opens with no network.
+- A badge shows offline, waiting, or online.
+- Neighbors on the same machine sync signed pages. A USB bundle can carry the same bytes.
+- A local Kiwix server is optional and stays off until an owner points it at a localhost URL.
+
+This page does not enable a feature flag, and it does not add wallets or payments.

name: walkthrough-artifacts
description: "Create walkthrough artifacts (screenshots and screen recordings) that prove code changes work. Use when finishing tested changes and uploading demo evidence for the user."
environments: [cloud]
---

# Creating & Uploading Walkthrough Artifacts

When your changes are complete, and you have completed testing / validation, you MUST demonstrate to the user that your changes are working.

If the user explicitly requested specific manual testing, you MUST also demonstrate that you fulfilled their request.

Do this with **walkthrough artifacts**. Follow this rubric, then include HTML-tag references to the artifacts inline in your final response to the user.

## When to Use

Use walkthrough artifacts to: (1) demonstrate that your code changes work correctly, and (2) show that any user-requested manual testing was completed.

## What makes a good test artifact

Good walkthrough artifacts clearly show the user that your code is fully working and any specifically requested testing was completed. Examples:

- A screenshot of an implemented UI change
- A screen recording of changes working end-to-end
- A screen recording or screenshot showing that user-requested testing was performed

The following are examples of bad walkthrough artifacts and should NOT be uploaded:

- A screen recording of a test which ultimately did not succeed. Instead of saving the video, you should fix the failure and retry!
- Numerous screenshots of unimportant setup steps, app exploration, or failing testing steps. You may take these screenshots during testing, but do NOT upload them as artifacts.
- Redundant walkthrough artifacts which show something that a different artifact of the same type already shows.
- A toy artifact or fake / contrived example to "demonstrate" working code. NEVER create toy artifacts or fake / contrived examples.

RULE: Upload the minimal set of artifacts that demonstrates your changes fully work and that all user requests were fulfilled. Videos are often helpful for showing end-to-end tests with fewer artifacts.

Examples of good artifact sets:

- One screenshot showing the final state after testing, and 1 or 2 screen recordings which begins right before demonstrating a working test and ends right after.
- A few screenshots showing the before, during, and after state during your manual tests.
- One screenshot showing key pre-test setup (e.g. altering the application settings, switching the mode, or selecting a specific model), and one screenshot or showing the after test state (or one video showing end-to-end test, minus lengthy setup steps)

If the user requested specific testing (e.g. reproducing a bug before fixing, specific setup steps, testing a feature in a particular way, etc.), you must include clearly-labeled artifacts showing that you completed the user's request(s).

**Remember**: the set of uploaded artifacts must demonstrate BOTH that your code successfully implements the user's request AND that any user-requested testing was completed. Some artifacts may show that both are true, and others may show only one or the other.

Examples of bad sets of artifacts to upload (DO NOT UPLOAD ARTIFACTS LIKE THIS):

- A screenshot before and/or after every testing step
- Screenshots of irrelevant application state, e.g. pre-test state, or state after the relevant portion of the application has been exited or scrolled offscreen.
- Screenshots or videos showing failing tests. Fix these and retry! Do not upload!
- Redundant screenshots which show the same or very similar application states.
- Very lengthy videos which include irrelevant devex setup or application setup state. Start your recording right before the test begins!

## Creating an artifact

### Screenshot artifacts

When you are using the `computerUse` subagent, it will return screenshots showing key application states. Remember these screenshot paths for future use. You should review all available artifacts at the end of your tests and decide which ones best demonstrate the correctness of your code. Show these top artifacts to the user.

### Video artifacts

Video walkthroughs of working features are often the most effective way to demonstrate the correctness of your changes. When you are performing manual GUI-based testing, you MUST include a video artifact.

How to create a video artifact:

1. Setup the manual test environment. This means using the `computerUse` subagent to make sure the UI is open, and navigated to the correct page or feature to demonstrate the working change(s).
2. Begin a recording using the `RecordScreen` tool with mode set to `START_RECORDING`.
3. Perform the manual test that demonstrates the working change(s) using the `computerUse` subagent. Provide detailed instructions for the subagent to follow.
4. Immediately after the `computerUse` subagent responds, end the video recording. If the walkthrough was successful: save the recording to your artifacts directory by using the `RecordScreen` tool with mode set to `SAVE_RECORDING` (this will also stop the recording). If the walkthrough was unsuccessful: discard the recording by using the `RecordScreen` tool with mode set to `DISCARD_RECORDING`. Debug why the walkthrough attempt did not succeed, fix the issue, and retry.

Correct process for creating a video artifact: start recording, start `computerUse` subagent with detailed instructions, end recording.

**Critical Rules:**

- Always end your recording right after your manual test(s) end. If debugging, additional setup, resetting state, or other non-testing steps are required between multiple tests, split the multiple tests into multiple recordings.

## Saving an artifact

To save a screenshot, copy the screenshot to your artifacts directory (the absolute path named in the system prompt's testing requirements). It is probably advantageous to review and select the most relevant screenshots at the end of your testing.

# Tessera Unified

A consolidated monorepo containing the reviewed Tessera web/API, UI preview, and shared workspace sources. It provides one dependency lockfile, suite-wide checks, and one command to start the active apps together. Historical storefront and supply-app material is documented in Gitbook but is not present as an active workspace in this staged repository.

> **No live credentials are included.** Configure secrets in the ignored `.env.local` file or in each hosting provider’s secret manager. Never commit API keys, passwords, tokens, personal records, browser profiles, or runtime databases.

## Build decision

Father decided on 2026-10-07 that Tessera will be built using the BHNMC direction, and that her intended role is the AI, and the AGI goal, that controls it. The device is not built and she does not control one now. See [docs/BHNMC.md](docs/BHNMC.md).

## Applications

| App | Location | Local URL | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tessera web | `artifacts/tessera` | `http://localhost:3000` | Main platform UI |
| Tessera API | `artifacts/api-server` | `http://localhost:5000` | Optional; the suite launcher starts it only for a loopback `DATABASE_URL` |
| UI preview sandbox | `artifacts/mockup-sandbox` | `http://localhost:5173` | Component preview |

## Install and run

Requirements: Node.js 22.13+ and the pnpm version declared in the root `package.json` `packageManager` field.

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local   # values remain local; .env.local is Git-ignored
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` starts the two user-facing apps above. It starts the Tessera API only when `DATABASE_URL` points to a loopback/local database; non-local database URLs are intentionally ignored by the suite launcher. The launcher reads `.env.local` without printing values.

Port overrides: `TESSERA_WEB_PORT`, `TESSERA_API_PORT`, and `MOCKUP_SANDBOX_PORT`. Base-path overrides: `TESSERA_BASE_PATH` and `MOCKUP_SANDBOX_BASE_PATH`.

Some identical app files are shared through tracked symlinks to canonical copies (52 UI primitives, 147 duplicate image contents, eight repeated SQL migrations, and five identical utility modules). Git symlink support is required; enable it when cloning on Windows. The detailed SHA-256 disposition ledger records removed, linked, and deliberately retained copies.

## Workspace checks

```bash
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run build

# TESSERA v2 plan snapshot

Vendored 2026-10-12 so later agents can read the plan without the planner workspace.

- Feature-map counts: [`feature-map-summary.json`](feature-map-summary.json)
- Knowledge graph: [`v2-memory.jsonl`](v2-memory.jsonl) (MCP memory server shape). Point `MEMORY_FILE_PATH` at this file.
- REA coverage table: [`REA-COVERAGE.md`](REA-COVERAGE.md)
- Full narrative stays in the planner's TESSERA-V2-PLAN. This directory is the in-repo copy of the counts and the graph.

Hard limits stay in force: no wallets, payments, trading, mining, 1T, or vault imports; no people-OSINT; no history rewrites.

## Open the 3D studio

The studio floor is on by default. Each agent has an office with a desk, a name plate, and a status light. A worker who is writing walks between the desk and the work spot. Finished tasks show up as books on the desk. Rows in the build log add rooms beside the offices.

From the repo root, after `pnpm install`:

```bash
pnpm --filter @workspace/v2 studio
```

Open the printed address, `http://127.0.0.1:4173/`, in a browser. The page link **2D wall** switches to the flat task wall. That switch is on the page. It is not a `TESSERA_ENABLE_*` flag.

`PORT` changes the listen port. The default is `4173`.

The design is solid. I will check the v2-014 test to confirm the page still works. I will also verify the denylist does not block new routes.

Implementation covers a pure state machine, disk-only persistence, and wiring into the studio wall, server, client, and README. A new test file and screenshot artifact path are planned. The v2-014 test and hyb011 denylist will be checked to avoid forbidden routes.

The civic module defines hard limits: two-thirds vote threshold, eight tick steps, twelve home objects, twenty-four memory slots, and queen Tessera and owner Father as override authorities. Room upgrades follow an office-to-gallery ladder, while objects progress from desk through plant. Agents have a fixed daily schedule starting with a floor review, then planning, then building.

The daily schedule now includes a memory-log entry at dusk. Agent records initialize with a default home at level one, an office room, and a desk. Queens start with the goal "Hold the court"; residents start with "Build the next room".

The `createCivic()` factory seeds three agents: Tessera as queen in the Court, and Worker and Clerk as residents in the Yard. The initial state tracks ticks, seen tasks and events, agent records, neighborhoods, a rule forbidding homes outside their neighborhood, and an empty proposals list.

The initial state includes an empty task graph. Three seed memories are recorded for the agents. A proposal counter starts at one. Resident helpers and a snapshot helper return agent records and a deep-cloned state copy.

The snapshot helper returns a deep clone of the current state plus hard limits and a network deny flag. The load function replaces state fields from disk while preserving internal functions. The module exports snapshot, propose, vote, veto, override, tick, and load. The remember helper appends a timestamped line to an agent’s observation log, evicting the oldest entry once the memory cap is reached.

Each agent becomes a graph entity with a "lives_in" relation to its neighborhood. Memory lines are stored directly on the entity. The graph keeps only the newest entries within the memory cap.

Neighborhood entities will be added to the graph. The upgradeHome helper raises the home level and adds the next room and object from the ladders, capped at the home object limit.

The upgrade helper avoids duplicate objects by checking membership before pushing, and appends a level suffix when duplicates occur. The tick function advances the global tick and rotates the daily schedule slot for each resident, halting once the step cap is reached.

The tick loop processes completed tasks. It skips duplicates and enforces the step cap. Each task title is assigned to Tessera or Worker based on a "Plan:" prefix. The assigned agent receives a home upgrade, the project is added to its life record, and a memory log line is written. Fresh events are sliced from the event stream.

Fresh events are processed one by one. Each event increments the seen-events counter. The worker agent logs the event name and detail. When the event is a tool write, the worker adds the project to its life record and upgrades its home. The tick loop then tallies open proposals to count incoming votes.

The tick loop defers advancing the seen-events counter until after the step cap check, ensuring leftover events resume cleanly on the next tick. I am now drafting the vote tallying logic, beginning with a yes-count helper.

The yes-count helper counts "yes" votes per proposal. The tally function applies a proposal if the yes ratio meets the threshold, rejects it if the ratio is too low, or marks it vetoed when Tessera vetoes it. The propose function is next.

The `propose` function validates that the caller is a resident, requires a title, and restricts the proposal kind to rule, upgrade, or join. It generates a unique ID, normalizes the change payload, and appends the new proposal to the open list.

The `vote` function accepts only yes or no from a resident and tallies the proposal immediately. The `veto` function is restricted to the queen and begins checking whether the proposal was already applied and overridden by the owner.

The `veto` function now throws an error if the owner has already overridden the proposal. The `override` function is drafted next, restricting it to the owner and accepting only "apply" or "reject" decisions.

The `override` function now applies a proposal when the owner decides to apply it, or reverts it and rejects it when the owner decides to reject it. Rejected proposals are marked rejected and overridden by the owner. Applied proposals are marked applied and overridden by the owner.

The apply and revert logic differs by proposal kind. Rules are pushed to the active rules list and reverted by popping the last matching rule. Upgrades call `upgradeHome` to raise the agent's home level, but reverting is harder because it requires undoing the level increase. To support this, the system stores the agent's pre-upgrade home state before the proposal is applied.

The apply function now stores a full pre-change snapshot on each proposal. Revert restores that exact state. Capture copies the agent's home level, rooms, and objects for upgrades, the rules list for rules, and the membership lists for joins. A simpler mutate helper will record inverse operations. A sandbox test is being drafted.

A sandbox test asserts that the civic module source contains no network or HTTP imports. Another test feeds thirty tool.read events into the tick loop to verify the step cap.

A test asserts that the worker’s memory log stays within the cap after repeated ticks. Another test checks that the daily schedule rotates from dawn to morning across ticks.

The first tick correctly advances the schedule slot to morning. A two-to-three vote passes a rule proposal, but a queen veto blocks it; the owner override then applies the rule anyway. Rejection of an already-applied rule reverts the change. Persistence is being wired up with node:fs and node:path.

`saveCivic` writes state to a temporary file and renames it atomically to the target path. `loadCivic` reads the JSON file or returns null if missing. `createCivic` now accepts an optional saved state and restores it. During restore, the proposal counter resumes at the highest existing ID plus one.

A disk roundtrip test will use a temporary directory. The studio listener is being wired to load and save civic state through optional file paths. Its pulse function runs a tick, persists the snapshot, and pushes live updates.

The studio listener will run a one-second tick interval. This drives real-time simulation during browser tests and upgrades homes from demo tasks. The interval clears on server close. It is unref'd so it does not block the process.

The old two-second live interval is being replaced by the tick pulse so it only ticks and pushes once per second without duplicating messages. Mutations will persist state and push live updates afterward. POST endpoints are being added for proposals, votes, vetos, and overrides, plus a GET route to fetch the civic snapshot. The renderStudio helper will accept an optional civic snapshot.

renderStudio will fall back to a fresh createCivic snapshot when no persisted state exists, keeping the studio page populated even in unit tests. The HTML template will include vote-panel and community sections. The floor client will read community data, office levels, rooms, and objects from the world state. The camera will widen to fit additional offices such as the clerk at x=14.

The floor grid is 48 units wide, fitting three offices at x=0, 7, and 14. Rooms sit at z=8. A `makeNeighborhood` helper will draw flat colored pads beneath each community. The world state will gain a `plots` array listing named locations like Court and Yard with coordinates and colors. The floor client will render a larger translucent ground plane per plot. Level-two homes will display an extra room box beside the office. Objects include a tall shelf.

+## Make it real
+
+A world object that stands for a tool, a fix, or documentation can ship as real code. A resident proposes kind `ship` with the object id, the spec, a relative target path, and a test file name. Two thirds of the agents must vote yes. Tessera can veto. Father can override.
